properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Illinois...

Thorn Creek at Thornton affecting Cook County.

For the Thorn Creek...including Thornton...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Thorn Creek from Near Glenwood downstream to confluence
with Little Calumet River, including the Thornton gauge.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Parking lots threatened at Glenwood
Academy.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM CDT Sunday the stage was 12.9 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:00 AM CDT Sunday was 13.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river has crested and is expected to fall below
flood stage early tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or
may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

These forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as
forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by late tonight.

properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to

properties.instruction:

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

dangerous flows in arroyos, ditches and over low water crossings. Do
not attempt to drive through areas where water covers the roadway.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 2 at 6:10PM MDT until August 2 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 610 PM MDT, local law enforcement reported people stranded due to
flash flooding in the Willow Creek subdivision.  More thunderstorms
are approaching the Sacaton and Hummingbird burn scars and may cross
between 630 and 730 PM with up to a half inch of additional rainfall.
Up to 1.3 inches of rain have already fallen. Flash flooding
continues and may get worse if additional rain falls.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Willow Creek and
Gilita Creek. This includes Willow Creek Road including the Ben Lilly
and Willow Creek Campgrounds and any other residences in this area.
Bursum Road near the Willow Creek Campground may also be impacted.
Middle Fork Trail number 157 and Iron Creek Trail number 172 will be
especially dangerous. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Sacaton and Hummingbird
burn scars.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Sacaton and Hummingbird burn scars.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Catron County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the Sacaton and Hummingbird burn scars. Severe debris flows can also
be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away
in places. If you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING FOR THE SACATON AND HUMMINGBIRD BURN SCARS REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 715 PM MDT THIS EVENING FOR SOUTH CENTRAL CATRON COUNTY

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 2 at 8:35PM EDT until August 2 at 9:45PM EDT by NWS Buffalo NY
properties.description:
For the following areas... Lake Erie from Dunkirk to the Buffalo
Harbor... The Upper Niagara River and Buffalo Harbor...

At 832 PM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from Small Boat Harbor to near Lake Erie Beach, moving east
at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
Small Boat Harbor, Lake Erie Beach, Wanakah, Woodlawn Beach, Erie
Basin Marina, Sturgeon Point, Athol Springs, Bayview, and Sunset Bay.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.
